title: Boiler Explosion at Andhra Pradesh Pharma Unit Kills Four, Injures Ten
excerpt: A boiler exploded at Till Healthcare's tablet-manufacturing plant in Sri City, Tirupati district, during the night shift, killing four workers and injuring at least ten. Rescue operations continued through the day as the state ordered a safety audit of the industrial zone.
body:
• A boiler exploded at Till Healthcare's tablet-manufacturing plant in the Sri City special economic zone of Tirupati district during the night shift on Saturday.
  • Four workers were killed, according to Andhra Pradesh officials; at least 10 others suffered serious injuries and were evacuated to hospitals in Tirupati and Chennai.
  • The blast triggered a fire inside the facility and caused structural damage; police, fire crews and emergency teams worked through the day on rescue and relief operations.
  • Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan ordered a comprehensive safety audit of all Sri City industries and promised government support for victims' families; the cause of the explosion remains under investigation.

Night-shift explosion at Sri City pharma unit

Four workers were killed and at least 10 others were seriously injured when a boiler exploded at a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in Sri City in the early hours of Saturday, officials said. The accident occurred at Till Healthcare's tablet-producing plant in the Sri City special economic zone, Satyavedu mandal, in Andhra Pradesh's Tirupati district, while workers were on the night shift.

https://x.com/IndiaToday/status/2106269211463237839

According to preliminary reports, the boiler suddenly exploded, triggering a massive fire inside the industrial unit and causing panic across the industrial area. Two workers died at the scene, officials said, and two others later succumbed to their injuries during treatment, taking the death toll to four. One seriously injured worker remains under medical care, while the others were shifted to hospitals in Tirupati and Chennai for treatment.

The powerful explosion caused structural damage to the facility. Police, fire department personnel and emergency teams rushed to the site, secured the premises and launched rescue and relief operations to evacuate trapped and injured workers. Authorities had not immediately released the identities of those killed, and the exact number of workers inside the unit at the time of the blast was still being ascertained.

A recurring pattern in India's pharma belt

The Sri City accident is the latest in a series of deadly industrial explosions in India's pharmaceutical manufacturing sector. The most severe came at a Sigachi Industries plant in Sangareddy district, Telangana, where a blast in a spray dryer unit killed at least 36 workers. Industrial boiler and pressure-equipment failures remain a persistent hazard: investigators typically examine maintenance records, operating procedures, pressure readings and safety systems to determine whether the cause was equipment failure, excessive pressure, an operational lapse or a technical malfunction.

Sri City, spread across the Andhra Pradesh-Tamil Nadu border, is one of India's largest integrated industrial hubs, hosting manufacturing units for electronics, automobiles and pharmaceuticals. Industrial safety in such zones is governed by the Boilers Act and state factories rules, but enforcement is uneven, and night-shift operations — when supervisory presence is thinnest — have repeatedly featured in fatal accidents.

Political response and relief measures

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and state minister Nara Lokesh expressed grief over the deaths and directed officials to extend full support to the affected families and ensure proper medical care for the injured.

"The deaths caused by the boiler explosion and the injuries suffered by several workers are deeply tragic."

— Nara Lokesh, Andhra Pradesh Minister for Education and IT

Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan spoke with the Tirupati district collector to review the situation and ordered a comprehensive safety audit of all industries within Sri City. He directed officials to ensure the injured receive the best medical treatment — one worker in critical condition was shifted to Apollo Hospital in Chennai — and assured victims' families that the coalition government would stand by them. He also called for a review of how safety standards are implemented across the zone to prevent similar accidents.

Diaspora angle

For Indians abroad, the blast lands in a region whose factories and hospitals are tightly linked to diaspora life: many Andhra Pradesh families have relatives working in the state's industrial corridors, and news of casualty figures that shifted through the morning — from two to four dead, with some early reports citing five — underscores why relatives overseas depend on verified, official casualty counts rather than viral speculation. The injured worker moved to Apollo Chennai also highlights how India's private tertiary-care network, long familiar to NRIs who return home for treatment, remains the backstop when district hospitals are overwhelmed.

What happens next

The exact circumstances leading to the explosion have not yet been established. An official working in the SEZ said investigators are expected to determine whether the accident resulted from a technical malfunction, a failure of safety systems, an operational lapse or another factor. The safety audit ordered by the deputy chief minister could set the scope of the inquiry, and officials will also have to address compensation for the families of the deceased and the injured — an issue that surfaced immediately in the government's public response. Further details, including the identities of the victims and the inquiry's findings, are expected in the coming days.
